A notch below 5 because Start's freshly-stable loader/head/server-fn calling conventions are woven through all eight route files, so an early-API change would touch every route.

justification.rationale: Every non-stable-forever API is either required by the spec (Start), the framework's documented way to ship a server (nitro RC — no stable v3 exists yet), or the current canonical API (.validator()). Nothing is used for novelty, and the app deliberately avoids RSC, React Compiler, and other previews it had no need for.

findings.issue: The production server is built by Nitro v3, which is still a release candidate (npm `latest` is 3.0.261029-rc, published 2026-10-29; no stable v3 exists — the RC blog post links 'Upgrading from Beta' breaking-change notes). Any breaking change between RC and stable would hit the build/start pipeline.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable, since this is exactly TanStack Start's documented path (its official start-basic example ships `nitro` as a devDependency too). Keep the lockfile pinned as-is and follow nitro.build's RC→stable migration notes when v3.0 final lands; consider a Dependabot/Renovate rule scoped to nitro.

findings.issue: @tanstack/react-start ^1.169.4 is the framework's first stable release (2026-10-13); all data loading runs through it, so early-API churn in the 1.169/1.170 line affects every route.
findings.suggestion: Nothing to change — it is the required framework at its current recommended version; just re-run the test suite on Start version bumps.

findings.issue: The 0.x package @tanstack/react-start-rsc rides along as a transitive dependency of react-start, even though the app uses no RSC features (no 'use client'/'use server' directives anywhere in src).
findings.suggestion: No action needed; noting it so a future RSC-related breaking change isn't mistaken for app code.

findings.issue: Vite 8 (Rolldown bundler) is a major architectural switch from Rollup-era Vite, stable since 2026-03-12 and required by Start 1.169.
findings.suggestion: Informational only; the pinned ^8.3.5 is current and mandated by the framework.

summary: The app's source code contains zero experimental markers — no unstable_/experimental_ names, no flags, no RSC directives — and its toolchain is a byte-for-byte match for TanStack Start's official current scaffold (Start 1.169.4, Router 1.170.46, Vite 8, nitro/vite). The residual risk is that this recommended stack is itself very new: Start 1.169 is the first stable release (17 days old) and nitro v3 is still an RC that builds the shipped server. All of it is confined to vite.config.ts, package.json and one server-fn wrapper module (app/src/lib/queries.ts), so a swap when RCs settle would be cheap.
